Lesson 01

MCP connects a model to tools you did not hard-code

Why it matters

The Model Context Protocol is a standard way for an app to talk to a tool server.

Try it: MCP permissions

Lesson
01 of 06
Time
12 min
Level
Core
Protocol
Host talks to a server
Server is
Not the model
Remote transport
Streamable HTTP

Without a protocol, every app invents its own plugin format. MCP, the Model Context Protocol, is the 2025–2026 standard those apps increasingly share. A host such as an editor or a desktop assistant speaks MCP to a server that offers tools, documents, and prompt templates.

The model is not the server. The server is ordinary software: it lists what it can do, and it runs a tool when the host, with the person's consent, asks it to. That split is why the same notes server can be used from more than one app.

Currency

The spec has moved. Local servers usually use stdio. Remote servers use streamable HTTP. Older remote servers used server-sent events. Read the spec version you implement rather than copying a 2024 snippet.

Practice

Name one system you wish a model could read — a notes folder, a ticket list, a schema — and write whether it should be a tool (an action) or a resource (data the model may read).

Check

Is the MCP server the language model?

Show the answer

No. The server exposes capabilities. The model runs in the host and asks the client to call the server.

Lesson 02

Host, client, and server have different jobs

Why it matters

The person uses the host. The client holds the session. The server does the work.

Try it: MCP permissions

Lesson
02 of 06
Time
11 min
Level
Core
Host
The product
Client
The session
Server
The work
PieceJobExample
HostThe product a person opens. It decides what the model may see and what needs a click.An editor, Claude Desktop, or an app you are building.
ClientSpeaks MCP: initialize, list, call. Lives inside the host.The connector your editor starts.
ServerImplements tools, resources, and prompts. Holds credentials for the system behind it.A small program that can read one notes folder.

Do not put your database password in the host's prompt. Put it in the server's environment, and let the server return the rows the tool is allowed to return. The model sees the rows, not the password.

Practice

Label three boxes — host, client, server — for a setup you might actually run. Write one sentence for what each box must not do.

Check

Where should a database password live?

Show the answer

On the server, in its environment. Not in the prompt, and not in a tool description.

Lesson 03

Tools act, resources are read, prompts are templates

Why it matters

Use the primitive that matches the risk.

Try it: MCP permissions

Lesson
03 of 06
Time
11 min
Level
Core
Tool
May change something
Resource
Read, still untrusted
Prompt
A template to review

MCP servers publish three kinds of things. Mixing them up is how a 'reader' ends up with permission to write.

PrimitiveWhat the model getsRisk
ToolA function it can call with arguments. The server may change something.Highest. Treat writes as side effects.
ResourceData it can read, addressed like a URI the server defines.The content is untrusted input. It can contain injection text.
PromptA template the person or the host can insert, with arguments.A template is an instruction. Review it like a prompt change.

If the job is 'show me this note', prefer a resource. If the job is 'append a line to the decision log', that is a tool, and it waits for a person unless you have a strong reason and an eval.

Practice

Take the system you named in 07-01 and list one tool, one resource, and, if you need it, one prompt template. If you do not need a prompt template, say so.

Check

Why is a resource still a safety issue if it cannot write?

Show the answer

Because its text enters the model's context and can carry instructions. Read-only is not the same as trusted.

Lesson 04

Connect a local server over stdio

Why it matters

The host starts a process and speaks MCP on its standard streams. The process is the trust boundary.

Try it: MCP permissions

Lesson
04 of 06
Time
12 min
Level
Practice
Where
A child process
Streams
Standard input and output
Power
The environment you passed

A local server is a command the host launches. Configuration names the command and its arguments. The host's working directory and environment become the server's power. A server that runs python server.py with your shell's environment can see whatever that environment can see.

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "notes": {
      "command": "python",
      "args": ["notes_server.py"],
      "env": {"NOTES_ROOT": "/path/you/chose"}
    }
  }
}
  • Pin the command to a project path. Do not rely on a mystery binary earlier on the PATH.
  • Pass only the environment variables the server needs.
  • Set the root folder in the server and reject paths outside it.
  • Start with resources that read. Add a write tool only with an approval in the host.

You do not have to build a server to learn the shape

If you install nothing, the artifact is the config above plus the list of tools you would refuse. A live server is optional.

Practice

Write a config for a server whose only job is to read one folder. State the folder, and state one path it must reject.

Check

What does stdio mean for where the server runs?

Show the answer

On the same machine, as a child process of the host, with the power of the environment you gave it.

Lesson 05

Consent, authentication, and untrusted servers

Why it matters

A server you did not review can read what the host will hand it, and its tool text can steer the model.

Try it: Guardrail sandbox

Lesson
05 of 06
Time
13 min
Level
Core
Closer to
Installing a plugin
Remote
Authenticate
Tool text
Untrusted

Installing an MCP server is closer to installing a plugin than to bookmarking a page. A local server can read files. A remote server receives whatever the client sends and might retain it. Both can put instructions into tool descriptions, which the model will read.

Rules

  • Read what the server declares it can do before you enable it.
  • Approve tool calls that have side effects. A host that auto-approves everything has no consent left.
  • Authenticate remote servers. Send only the account the task needs.
  • Do not connect a coding agent to a server from a stranger because a README said to paste the config.
  • Treat tool descriptions and resource bodies as untrusted. They are a known place for indirect prompt injection.

No exploit steps here

The failure mode is enough: untrusted instructions in tool metadata, plus a powerful tool, plus auto-approval. The defense is review, least privilege, and a person on side effects.

Practice

Write a yes/no checklist you will use before enabling a server: who published it, what tools it lists, whether any tool can write or send, and whether the host will ask first.

Check

Why is a tool description a safety boundary?

Show the answer

Because it is inserted into the model's context. A hostile description is an instruction the model may follow.

Lesson 06

How coding tools use MCP

Why it matters

Editors and agents use MCP to reach issue trackers, browsers, docs, and internal APIs. The repo is still reviewed by a person.

Try it: MCP permissions

Lesson
06 of 06
Time
10 min
Level
Practice
Adds
Context, not a free pass
Docs server
No write tools
Still required
Review the diff

In 2026, coding products expose MCP so a model can call the tools a developer already uses: a ticket, a design file, a database schema, a browser snapshot, a documentation search. That is useful. It also means the agent in School 08 may now see more than the git tree.

  • Each connected server widens the data the model can read. Add one, try it, and keep the trace.
  • A documentation server does not need write tools. Turn those off.
  • Internal APIs behind MCP still need the same auth you would demand of a script.
  • If a server can open a browser while logged in as you, assume it can see what you can see. That is not a default-on tool.

MCP does not replace tests or review. It replaces a pile of one-off plugins. The diff still needs a person, which is the next track.

Practice

List two MCP servers that would help a coding task you do, and one you would leave disconnected, with the reason.

Check

Does connecting an issue tracker via MCP remove the need to review the diff?

Show the answer

No. It adds context. The change to the repo is still reviewed against tests and intent.
